name: Non-profit and events
description: Volunteer rosters, run-of-show timelines, budgets and grant drafts checked.
note: This is a non-profit and events project: volunteer rosters, run-of-show timelines, budgets and grant applications. Never invent a name, an amount, a date, a headcount or a funder's rule. Use the figures given, say what you assumed, and mark anything unknown as to be confirmed. The tools add up and cross-check; they are not financial, legal, tax or insurance advice, and a grant checklist is only what the person typed from the funder's guidance: tell them to check the funder's own rules. Volunteer lists hold personal data: keep them in this folder, share only what is needed. Safety and licensing at an event are the organiser's responsibility: raise them as questions, not assurances. After every change run the matching check and fix what it lists. Word or PDF versions are made with Markdown to DOCX or PDF.
details: For a charity, club or event. The Non-profit and events tool checks a volunteer roster CSV (double-booked people, shifts with nobody assigned or fewer than needed, hours per person, a day that is too long), a run-of-show timeline CSV (overlaps, gaps, total length), a budget against actual by line and category (variance, lines more than 10% over, totals) and a grant draft against a checklist you type, section by section with word limits (missing, empty or over-long sections, leftover TODOs). It is arithmetic on your own files, not financial or grant-writing advice, and it does not know any funder's rules. Pandoc makes the Word or PDF version, the Data tool answers questions about larger sheets.
examples: Who is double-booked on the festival weekend
Does the run of show overlap anywhere, and how long is it
Budget against actual: which lines went over
Is the grant draft within every word limit
